articleTitle: Development of an Improved Control System for Active Rectifiers with Additional Negative Sequence Currents Control Loops
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: Modern main electric drives of rolling mills are performed using asynchronous (synchronous) AC electric motors and three-level frequency converters with active rectifiers and autonomous voltage inverters. Semiconductor switches are controlled by pulse width modulation method with orientation by the supply voltage vector. AR control systems are sensitive to the quality of the mains voltage. Occurrence of voltage sags in the mains leads to FC-AR emergency shutdowns. AR emergency shutdown occurs due to the increase in the voltage swing in the DC link and the increase in the currents consumed by FC, which is caused by the flow of reverse sequence currents. In this connection, the actual task is the development of measures to improve the stability of the main electric drives of the mill at voltage perturbations on the part of the electric power system. The paper develops an improved AR control system with an additional control loop of orthogonal components of the reverse sequence currents to improve the AR operation reliability under asymmetrical voltage dips by maintaining the reverse sequence currents on active and reactive components equal to zero for the entire duration of the voltage dips.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Implication of Fishing Substation Voltage on Energy Efficiency of Mechanized Oil Production
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The outgoing line of the field substation feeding the electrotechnical complex of producing wells is considered. Analytical expressions have been obtained for calculating the operating parameters of a submersible electric motor, which is powered through a control station equipped with a frequency converter. Refined expressions are presented for calculating the active and reactive power consumed by a submersible asynchronous electric motor and losses in a step-up transformer, taking into account the influence of the inclusion of frequency converters in the power supply circuit. An example is given of calculating the best voltage value of a field substation, at which minimum specific energy consumption is possible during mechanized oil production for a hypothetical outgoing line feeding an electrical complex of producing wells for two variants of the power supply scheme: without frequency converters and with a frequency converter in one of the control stations. The conclusion is made about the influence of the equipment of the control station.

articleTitle: Research on the Use of Amorphous Steel in an Electric Motor for UAVs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: Research on the use of amorphous steel in an electric motor for UAVs is the object of this scientific article, the application means the manufacture of sheets for the subsequent assembly of a magnetic circuit for ED-BAS-4950/400. A comparison of the effectiveness of using a soft magnetic amorphous material relative to the initially selected and previously used cold-rolled electrical steel 2421 in the electric motor for the UA V ED-BAS-4950/400 is the subject of this scientific article. Full-scale tests are carried out, including the following works: measurement of the active resistance and inductance of the stator winding; removal of the dependence of the counter-EMF on the speed of the electric motor; testing of the electric motor under load with an air screw; determination of the idle moment in generator mode. To conduct field tests, 4 experimental samples of ED-BAS-4950/400 electric motors are being manufactured, two samples of which contain magnetic cores made of amorphous steel, the other two samples contain magnetic cores made of electrical steel 2421.

articleTitle: Research of the Spacer Layers' Material Variation Impact on the Resonant-Tunneling Diode's Current-Voltage Characteristic
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The impact of indium doping percentage in resonant-tunneling diode's spacer layer on the diode's current-voltage characteristic was assessed by the means of computer modeling. The previously developed resonant-tunneling diode's physical and topological model has been supplemented with the parameters required for diffusion processes modeling in the active region of the diodes with InGaAs spacer layers. It is shown that with 20% substitution of gallium by indium in the studied resonant-tunneling diode's spacer layers, the peak current of the current-voltage characteristic's initial section increases approximately by 5 times, the peak voltage - approximately by 2 times. The peak current's and peak voltage's dependencies on the indium doping percentage in the resonant-tunneling diode's spacer layers were obtained. From the results of the study, it was concluded that it is promising to include the resonant-tunneling diode's spacer layers' chemical composition in the controlled parameters of the diode's design parameters optimization to achieve the required electrical characteristics.

articleTitle: A Robotic Milling Center for Orthoses and Prostheses Forms Production
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The article discusses the robotic center for orthoses and prostheses forms production, the problems of creating a control program in the SprutCAM system in terms of accuracy and running speed. A large number of points in the robot's trajectory certainly allows for more accurate processing of the product. A large number of frames can significantly slow down the actual processing of the product, regardless of the feed specified in the program, since the processing of each point requires a certain resource. Changing the number of frames in the direction of decreasing due to the improvement of mathematical accuracy, the actual processing accuracy did not deteriorate, the processing time corresponded to the calculated time.

articleTitle: Development of the Theory of Spline-Algebraic Harmonic Analysis as Applied to Navigation Radio Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: As is known, the main methods for increasing the noise immunity of navigation radio signals are spectral methods, the development of new and improvement of existing signal-code structures, algorithms for generating and processing radio signals. This article presents a new approach to the generation of GNSS GLONASS navigation radio signals based on the theory of basis function systems, where the basis function itself is used as a manipulation parameter. The obtained results of assessing the computational complexity of the proposed approach allow us to assert that the speed of processing radio signals in various basis functions can be significantly higher compared to similar processing of classical radio signals in discrete exponential functions.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Power Consumption Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The article proposes a model for medium-term forecasting of daily active power schedules in Moscow, it is formed on the basis of machine learning using a regression decision tree algorithm, taking into account average daily data on air temperature, cloudiness and natural light. This model predicts the values of daily electricity consumption time series taking into account meteorological factors based on simple decision rules derived from the characteristics of the data. The initial data were archives of average daily values of electricity consumption time series, air temperature, cloudiness and natural light for the territory of Moscow for the period from January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2019. Forecasts of average daily active power values were made using a forecast model based on the decision tree method for selected periods in April, June and October. The results of forecasting the active powers average daily values show that in most test examples the values obtained were no more than 5%. In addition, the developed algorithm allows the use of seasonal patterns between daily active power schedules and meteorological factors. Software implemented as a modeling tool was Python.

articleTitle: Increasing the Energy Characteristics of Three-Phase Asynchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The issues of saving fuel and energy resources at the present stage seem to be pivotal in the development of the economic activity of the state. The natural process of scientific and technological progress includes the increasing limitation of natural resources and an increase in the consumption of various types of energy. The article presents theoretical questions and shows the results of research to determine some of the possibilities for improving the energy efficiency of numerous and diverse consumers of electric energy - asynchronous motors. In addition, the authors obtained a patent for an invention, the use of which makes it possible to increase the energy performance of asynchronous motors operating with a low load factor.

articleTitle: Simulation of Call Center Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The article is devoted to evaluating call center performance by developing a simulation program. The call center is presented as a queuing system with waiting and rejection. A two-level predictive call routing algorithm has been introduced into the program. The functions of the expert level are performed by a separate group of specialists. The presence of interactive voice menu is also taken into account. The recursive method of searching for a free network resource is used. The data processing is simulated on the example of a network model of distributed call service centers. The result is the receipt of the estimated probabilistic-temporal parameters for performance evaluation according to the statistical data of the monitoring system. The user interface of the program and the initial data input window on the network model are presented. Both the network structure and the number of switching nodes in the network model can be changed at the request of the program users. The program allows to build and display various plots of time dependence on the monitor screen. As an example, the article provides a series of dependency graphs for determining the probability of service denial according to the current algorithm.

articleTitle: Specifics of Mathematical Modeling of Various Types of Wind Turbines in ARM SRZA and RastrKZ Software Packages
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: Recently, many countries have been commissioning large numbers of wind power plants (WPP) with wind turbines (WT) The development of power output diagrams for WPPs is associated with problems of the mathematical modeling of WTs for the calculation of short-circuit (SC) currents. This is required for the selection of relay protection (RP) device setting parameters. Some software packages (SP) use verified WT models with automated control and protection systems that correctly account for their operating modes. The ARM SRZA and RastrKZ software packages lack the capacities for the correct mathematical modeling of WTs, although they can calculate the periodic component of the SC current in the initial moment. The lack of methodological guidelines for the mathematical modeling of WTs in the ARM SRZA and RastrKZ SP results in the incorrect rendering of WTs as synchronous generators. This results in the insufficient sensitivity of RP startup units, their non-selective operation, and unnecessary shutdowns of the WTs by the LVRT function when the RP operates correctly. The electromechanical transient processes calculated in the PowerFactory DIgSILENT SP showed that the periodic component of the SC current contribution from WTs attenuates over 100 ms max. When modeling WTs in the ARM SRZA and RastrKZ SP, the authors suggest setting the current source as an EMF Behind the Resistance voltage source with respective parameter recalculation. The comparison of calculations for the periodic component of the SC current contribution from type I, II, III, and IV WTs, performed in the PowerFactory DIgSILENT software, as well as the ARM SRZA and RastrKZ SP showed that the difference is within 10% according to the suggested approach.

articleTitle: Development of a Synchronous Electric Motor with Permanent Magnets for Small-Sized Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The development and manufacture of a synchronous electric motor with permanent magnets for small-sized UAVs has been carried out. The results of the main stages performed during the creation of an electric machine and including the structural, computational and experimental parts are presented. The choice of the type and appearance of the electric motor design, as well as the materials from which its elements are made, was carried out in the structural part. In the calculation part, the size of the active part, the type of winding and the calculation of the performance characteristics of an electric machine were performed using electromagnetic modeling in the Ansys Motor-CAD software package. The test results of the manufactured sample and its closest analogue are given in the experimental part. The developed electric motor, when compared, showed output indicators close to the analog.

articleTitle: A Two-Phase Monopolar Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: Brushless monopolar generators are a new type of electrical machines developed by the authors. A new design of a previously known two-phase monopolar generator is proposed, and the generator operating modes for linear and nonlinear loads in a wide range of parameters are investigated. The results obtained allow to evaluate the prospects for application in industry. The power supply mode from two phases to a three-phase load is also investigated, with a symmetrical shift of 120 degrees on the load when powered by a three-wire circuit. Thus, the generator design is simple and can be used to power two-phase and three-phase loads. The absence of brushes ensures long-term maintenance-free operation and high reliability.

articleTitle: Impact of Resistive Neutral Grounding on Arcing During Single-Phase Faults in Low-Voltage Electric Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: This article considers the safety improvement possibilities of low-voltage three-phase electric networks by grounding their neutral through a high-value resistor. The safety of an electric network is primarily determined by single-phase fault processes. Arcing faults are the most dangerous type of such processes. The conducted research showed that low-voltage grounding arcs are unstable. Arc duration does not exceed half of the free current period of the single-phase fault. Such arcing faults result in overvoltages and heat production at the insulation damage location. This paper considers the features of arcing in low-voltage electric networks with neutral grounded through a resistor. These features were studied in physical experiments. During the experiments, the authors recorded the electric arc current and voltage oscillograms. The obtained oscillograms were used to assess the power and maximum current surges of the grounding arc. The authors studied the impact of three-phase electric network parameters like the impedance of the resistor connected to the neutral, phase capacitance, and voltage value on the power of the arc. Experiments were conducted on a physical model of an electric network with voltages of 220 V and 380 V. The results were compared with similar research on electric networks with an insulated neutral and showed. This showed that high-value resistor grounding of the neutral can be effectively used to improve the safety of low-voltage electric networks.

articleTitle: Current Trends in Modernization of Stator Design of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: In today's world, when permanent magnet synchronous motors are becoming more and more popular, the issue of optimizing their design becomes especially important. Such motors have a number of advantages over induction motors, but their main disadvantage is their high cost. The purpose of this paper is to study the current trends in modernization of motor design and to develop a method of multicriteria topological optimization of the stator design of a permanent magnet synchronous motor using a genetic algorithm. Applying a genetic algorithm to optimize the design improves the accuracy of the calculations compared to alternative methods such as simple brute force and is less time consuming than traditional finite element approaches. A key aspect of the optimization is to reduce the amount of materials used in the production of the engine without sacrificing power.

articleTitle: Structural Synthesis Features of Engineering Solutions for Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: Structural synthesis of innovative engineering solutions (ES) for renewable energy (RE) requires high competence and creativity on the part of engineers and designers, as well as effective teamwork. It aims to create technical products that will meet market needs, be competitive and bring economic benefits. It involves analyzing user needs, market research and technical evaluation of possible solutions, selection of the best option and development of specific technical solutions. Morphological approach of engineering solutions is a method of studying the structure and interrelationships between different elements of the system. The approach allows identifying key attributes and options necessary for successful implementation. The paper discusses the use of the morphological approach as applied to the synthesis of technical solutions in the subject area using examples. A number of examples are used to illustrate the approach.

articleTitle: Design of Frequency-Controlled Electric Drive with Proportional-Integral-Differential Regulator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The desire to increase the efficiency and reliability of industrial facilities contributes to the development of new technical solutions aimed at modernizing equipment. This work presents the design of a variable-frequency electric drive using a proportional-integral-derivative controller to control a main pumping unit. Using such a system allows you to reduce energy consumption and reduce the frequency of unexpected repairs. The simulation was carried out using the Matlab/Simulink package, which ensured precise tuning of the proportional-integral-derivative controller adapted to pressure changes. As a result of the simulation, diagrams of the parameters of the constituent elements of the system were obtained. After analyzing the diagrams, one can judge the possibility of operating a variable-frequency electric drive of a synchronous electric motor, since this method of controlling a synchronous electric motor is the most effective.

articleTitle: Protection of Hexagon Connections Using Reed Switches and Microprocessors with Majority Scheme and Functional Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The necessity to improve the reliability of relay protection for connections at open switchgear with voltages of 110–750 kV is substantiated. It is shown that to achieve this, it is advisable to use the majority method, duplicating current transformers with reed switches. The properties of reed switches are described, and their advantages are highlighted in comparison with the use of other magnetic-sensitive elements. For connections of open switchgear configured in a hexagon scheme, a general backup protection is proposed, with one of the sets based on the principle of comparing the power sign on a microprocessor and current transformers, and the other two based on the use of Kirchhoff's law, a microprocessor, and reed switches, but without current transformers. The protection scheme is provided, and its behavior in various operating modes is examined. It is shown that such protection will be much more reliable and economical than previously proposed solutions.

articleTitle: Automation for Quality Assessment of Refined Petroleum Using Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The selective petroleum derivative refining technology is used extensively in the industrial production of refined pe-troleum. The manufacturing of quality lubricants depends on the stable quality of products obtained with the selective refining unit. The quality of petroleum oil as a product of selective refining of input oil is provided by controlling a number of refining unit operation parameters. These parameters include extraction temper-ature, N-methylpyrrolidone (extraction agent) concentration, etc. The effective values of these parameters are mainly determined by the chemical composition of the input oil. The quality of the obtained refined petroleum is controlled using a flow refractometer with readings confirmed by regular sampling and laboratory tests. One of the problems with such verification is the duration of la-boratory tests when off-spec products can be produced, leading to re-processing costs, etc. This paper suggests using a neural network-based IT solution for the analysis of flow refractometer readings adequacy. The neural network was trained on sets of flow refractometer data obtained at different times and confirmed by laboratory tests during the refining of one material type. The nu-merical experiment showed that the trained neural network can very accurately predict the refraction coefficient for normal refining. Simultaneously, the neural network can easily detect deviations that can be caused by various factors.

articleTitle: The Use of Power Decoupling Method and Sliding Mode Current Controllers for Virtual Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The article discusses a voltage source inverter control system based on a virtual synchronous machine. Methods of improving a current control virtual synchronous machine known in the literature are proposed - the interdependence of the output active and reactive power is eliminated by changing the algorithm for generating set currents, and the quality of regulation and the harmonic composition of the output electricity are improved by replacing PI current regulators with sliding type regulators. The approbation and confirmation of the claimed properties of the designed control system was carried out using the Matlab/Simulink and the Simscape library.

articleTitle: Improvement of Corrective Agents Dispensing Control Systems for Thermal Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The paper is devoted to corrective agents dispensing control systems for thermal power plants, namely, hydrazine dispensing control system and phosphates dispensing control system. The systems mentioned are single-loop systems with PI-algorithms and they do not work efficiently enough now. Traditional variants of these system and their improvements earlier offered are described. Some new improvements, are offered and analyzed. They are prediction module using and control algorithm tuning parameters optimization. The prediction module uses the linear prediction algorithm. The transient processes and Nyquist curves for the control systems are given and analyzed. The quality indexes for the control systems are calculated. All the calculations are based on experimental data given in the papers already published.

articleTitle: The Use of Production Process Factors for the Short-Term Load Forecasting of the Compressor Station of the Main Gas Pipeline
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The forecasting of the power consumption of the Gad Industry enterprises can allow to equalize the schedule of power consumption, optimize the operation modes of objects of own generation and storage systems of electrical energy, optimize the maintenance and repair schedule and processes of other supporting systems, minimize the cost of the use of power consumption. The object of this article is the compressor station of the main gas pipeline. The issue of forecasting the power consumption of the compressor station is more complicated than forecasting the load curve of a large system due to the less periodicity of the power consumption, its greater variance, and the need to consider factors of the production process. The novel usage of production process factors for the forecasting of the power consumption of the compressor station of the main gas pipeline was introduced. In the article, two experiments with different feature combinations were conducted. The need for consideration of factors of the production process was discussed. It was shown that using these factors reduces the mean absolute error from 105 kWh (mean absolute percentage error is 16.81%) obtained using expert prediction, up to 15.52 kWh (3.44%) obtained using the ensemble machine learning method. The application of the SHaply Additive exPlanation algorithm for the interpretation of the results of short-term load forecasting was presented.

articleTitle: Creation of Synchronous Wind Generators Size Spectrum for the Russian Arctic Region
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: Various methods of creating a power size spectrum R10 of permanent magnets synchronous wind generators for Russia Arctic region in the range of 400-1250 kW have been investigated. Synchronous generators realize the well-known advantages of concentrated windings over distributed windings and the magnetic flux concentration. The synchronous generator of 800 kW power is selected as the base machine. For a size spectrum of wind generators with a single-stage gearbox, a pattern of changes in the generators rotation frequency has been obtained. It is established that the required power size spectrum is realized at three diameters, six lengths and three rotational speeds. By choosing two values of the base rotation speed, two size spectra are obtained. The geometric dimensions and electromagnetic parameters regularities of a combined size spectrum of 12 generators are investigated.

articleTitle: Application of Quadrature Demodulation to Measure the Parameters of Polyharmonic Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: One of the alternatives to the discrete Fourier transform for complex spectrum measurement problems is the quadrature demodulation method. The main advantage of this approach is the high accuracy of measuring both the parameters of the complex spectrum and the frequency. The disadvantages include a significant increase in the complexity of implementation associated with the use of a digital filtering device. Like the discrete Fourier transform, the quadrature demodulation method allows you to obtain amplitude, phase values and frequency for both sinusoidal and polyharmonic input signals. In this article, the case of a polyharmonic input signal is considered. Analytical dependences have been obtained to estimate the measurement error of the amplitude value, frequency and initial phase for a signal of this type. The requirements for the output filters of the demodulator are worked out, the relationship between the filter parameters and the measurement error of the considered signal parameters is shown. The question of the influence of the spectral composition of the signal and the final measurement error is investigated. The complexity of the implementation of such an approach is estimated for the case of measuring the parameters of polyharmonic signals. Schematic and algorithmic methods for reducing the measurement error of these parameters are proposed. The results of the study were verified using simulation mathematical modeling in the Matlab software package.

articleTitle: Optimizing Electric Vehicle Charging Station Placement in Distribution Systems for Enhanced Power Grid Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The integration of electric vehicles in the transportation sector leads to lessening greenhouse gas emissions. It is mandatory to recharge electric vehicles as it depends on the battery storage system and due to the increase in electric vehicles models and numbers, there is a need for installing electric vehicles charging stations to meet new load needs that are considered as an overload. The unscheduled placement of electric vehicles charging stations harms the power grid and leads to poor power quality. This paper presents a proposed algorithm to optimally allocate electric vehicles charging stations in a distribution system. The allocation is based on minimizing the energy loss and maintaining the system voltage profile within limits. This is accomplished by considering a variable load profile and the charging/discharging profile of electric vehicles charging stations. To support system voltage, Vehicle-to-Grid mode is applied instead of using additional energy source. MATLAB/Simulink® software package and genetic algorithm are used to verify the proposed algorithm on a standard distribution network. The results prove the algorithm reliability as the system load is approximately doubled, and energy loss is barely slightly increased.

articleTitle: Impact of Gravitational Anomalies and Vertical Deviations on the Accuracy of Inertial Navigation Systems and Compensation Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The accuracy of Inertial Navigation Systems (INS) has significantly improved, making previously negligible sensor errors, such as gravitational disturbances, major sources of errors. This paper analyzes the impact of gravitational anomalies on various stages of position calculation in INS and their influence on accuracy. The study includes the examination of gravitational disturbances using spherical harmonic decomposition and Legendre series, employing models like EIGCN-6C4 and WGS-84. It also explores the impact of these disturbances on initial alignment, the overall INS navigation process, and methods for compensating gravitational disturbances. Finally, simulations are conducted to validate the proposed hypotheses. This comprehensive analysis aims to enhance the understanding of gravitational disturbances and improve the accuracy and reliability of INS through detailed simulations and practical solutions.

articleTitle: Approbation of the Software Bundle for Wind Energy Calculations “Wind Energy PRO”
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The paper presents the development and validation of the “Wind Energy PRO” software bundle, a comprehensive tool designed for wind energy calculations. This software was created to provide a user-friendly alternative for engineering professionals and educational institutions. “Wind Energy PRO” encompasses multiple modules, including those for wind energy cadastre calculation, vertical interpolation of wind speed, wind turbine energy yield calculation, and wind farm energy yield calculation. These features collectively enable detailed analysis and optimization of wind energy projects. The validation of “Wind Energy PRO” was conducted using operational data from the Adygeyskaya wind farm in Russia. The results of this validation process demonstrated the software's high level of accuracy and effectiveness in modeling wind resources and predicting energy yield. This indicates its strong potential for practical application in real-world wind energy projects. The findings suggest that “Wind Energy PRO” is capable of reliably assessing wind energy potential, optimizing wind farm performance, and thereby serving as a practical tool for stakeholders in the wind energy sector.

articleTitle: Analysing the Peculiarities of Power Supply of Low-Current Systems for Controlling Small-Scale Generation Facilities
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: Automation and digitalization of the surrounding space leads to the development of management systems and reduces the risks of harm to the environment and human health. However, the operation of these systems is possible only if certain parameters of the power supply network are provided. If the quality indicators of electric energy deviate, there is a risk of malfunctions and accidents in the operation of equipment, which can lead to serious consequences for both equipment and people. This is possible when using power supplies or high-power frequency regulators, which can be sources of higher harmonics in the network. In this regard, there is a need to assess and minimize their impact on the enterprise's power supply system at the design stage. Unsatisfactory indicators of electricity quality lead to an increase in losses in power supply systems and a decrease in the service life of equipment. There is a need to increase capital investments in construction and repair, and operating costs increase.

articleTitle: Aging Mechanisms of Transformer Oils and Their Aging Markers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: Transformer oils (TO) are used for filling power and instrument transformers, reactor equipment, and oil switches. During the operation of a transformer, profound changes occur in the transformer oil, which are usually called aging. The article discusses the features of the luminescence spectra of transformer oils of different brands (GK, T -1500, TKp), oils with different dielectric loss tangents and acid numbers (AN) (with different degrees of aging). The purpose of the study is to develop new markers of aging of transformer oil, using changes in the composition of aromatic compounds in it and associated changes in the luminescence spectra of these oils. Based on the analysis of literature data and conducted research, the dependence of the luminescence spectra of oils on the brand of oils has been established; it has been shown that in the series of oils GK, T -1500, TKp, the concentration of complex aromatic compounds increases, which leads to a shift in the luminescence spectra of oils towards longer wavelengths. During the aging process of oils, the concentration of aromatic compounds also increases and their structure of molecules of aromatic compounds changes, the intensity of luminescence of transformer oil increases, as well as a shift in the luminescence spectra of oils to the red region of the spectrum. Aromatic compounds as a marker based on luminescence spectra make it possible to determine the brand of transformer oil, the degree of aging of oils, and can also be used in the regeneration of oils to determine the degree of aging.

articleTitle: Methodology for Increasing the Lifetime of Submersible Electric Motors in Power Supply Systems of Production Wells
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: An accident database for submersible electrical installations (SEIs) with submersible electric motors (SEM) in the Volga region has been compiled and subjected to analysis. The impact of each technological violation within the overall chain of failures, stemming from a complex interplay of external and internal processes involving SEI objects, is being assessed. Simultaneously, various external operational physical influences and internal processes, notably aging and operational irregularities, either individually or, most frequently, in diverse combinations, tend to diminish the capacity of a given SEI object, in particular SEM, to withstand the depletion of its internal resources. The described methodology allows for the identification of properties related to the randomness of SEMs failure processes, which may not be discernible through conventional real-time monitoring. The advantages and disadvantages of approaches to organizing the operation of SEMs based on operating time and actual condition during planning, implementation of maintenance and repair, as well as the feasibility of their integrated use are assessed. It is proposed to use statistical models to make a reasoned decision on determining the composition and period of maintenance and repair, forecasting the boundary states of sets in general and specific electrical installations of SEMs. The methodology for implementing vibroacoustic diagnostics in the assessment of SEMs within oil production enterprises (OPEs) is being examined.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Model for System-of-Systems Interoperability
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The article discusses the role of digitalization and the Internet of Things (IoT) in today's world, with a focus on their application in industrial automation as part of the Industry4.0 concept. A case is made for the use of IoT to improve monitoring, increase production flexibility and save resources. Particular attention is given to systems of systems (SoS), which consist of autonomous and interacting components. Five key characteristics of SoS are examined: autonomy, ownership, connectivity, diversity, and emergence. The paper also analyzes service-oriented architectures (SOAs), such as RAMI4.0 and OPC-UA, which are used to integrate IoT and SoS. The importance of developing interfaces and service contracts to enable interoperability between system components is discussed. A separate section is devoted to cyber-physical systems (CPS), which combine physical and computational elements to create more complex and interconnected industrial systems. The paper discusses the different classes of interoperability: informational, semantic, dynamic, and operational, and their role in the design and operation of SoS. It concludes by proposing the application of network control principles SPCFA to SoS system management, which contributes to improved monitoring and control in industrial automation.

articleTitle: Voltages in Disconnected Overhead Transmission Line, Induced by Electric and Magnetic Field of Operated Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The paper proposes the algorithm for calculation of voltages in phases and wire of parallel disconnected overhead transmission line induced by electric and magnetic field of operating in coordinated load mode overhead transmission line. Two single-circuit 220 kV lines were taken as the studied ones. Disconnected line protected phase and part length in which this phase should be protected (1 km) are selected. This section is grounded by the ends to line towers. Disconnected line all other phases and lightning wires are grounded to one tower inside the protected area. Electric field effects determine by capacitive currents in grounding phases, wires, grounding devices and in the ground. Magnetic field effects determine by current in the circuit of protected phase and the generated in phases and wires part grounded by one side s longitudinal electromotive force. Equations for voltage distribution over the ground along each phase and wire in the protected and non-protected areas finding are compiled according to electric and magnetic impact schemes. Resulting voltage distribution along each part determine by received voltages electrical and magnetic components adding.

Author Keywords: operated and disconnected overhead transmission line
voltages between phase/wire and ground and between phases/wires along disconnected line

articleTitle: Application of Ferrimagnetic Element Chiral Properties for Ferroprobe Excitation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The paper is concerned with the ferroprobe excitation system characteristics. The research objective is to improve the measuring accuracy and the ferroprobe technological parameters due to significant reduction in the thermal disturbing factor, interference resistance improvement and simplification of the ferrobrobe modulator design. This is achieved by the fact that the change in the ferrimagnetic core magnetic state is carried out by means of a modulator, the ferrimagnetic core is affected perpendicular to its longitudinal symmetry axis by the alternating electric field, which excites a standing modulating transverse electric (TE) wave or a magnetic-type H wave in the core on the modulator resonance frequency. In addition, the modulator resonant mode is set up so that 3/2 of the standing excited wave length could get through the ferrimagnetic core length and its mean antinode could be located on the transverse symmetry axis of the ferrimagnetic core. To implement this method, the radiating dipole element covering a part of the ferromagnetic core length is designed in the form of the C-antenna. The specified antenna consists of two separate current-conducting elements in the form of lateral faces of thin-walled semi-cylinders attached symmetrically to the external surface of the thin-walled dielectric cylinder bushing and aligned by its bigger side along its element and located symmetrically in relation to the ferrimagnetic core transverse symmetry axis. At the same time, the core also acts as an adjusting element of the C-antenna operating mode and the modulation element of the measured constant magnetic field.

articleTitle: Decentralized Management Protocol for Wireless Sensor Network in Industrial Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The paper comprises construction and evaluation of a decentralized management protocol in a self-organizing decentralized wireless sensor network (WSN) within the framework of the Industrial Internet of Things. The protocol is focused on organizing and supporting the functioning and monitoring of the information security of the network in order to collect, process, store and analyze data from the WSN nodes in conditions of high dynamism and variability of the network structure, the set of the nodes, their physical location in space, the behavior of the nodes and the amount of their available resources. This paper focuses on three proposed basic algorithms that constitute this protocol, their essence and analysis. In particular, it reveals the features of two alternative protocols for forming a multilateral session of WSN nodes, which provides a secure decentralized network operation using a node role model and blockchain as a means to organize distributed secure data storage on WSN nodes. In addition, the proposed protocol is oriented to solve the problems of monitoring the information security of a self-organizing decentralized wireless sensor network and detecting attacks that exploit, particularly, the properties of self-organization and decentralization of the network.

articleTitle: Alternative Protections on Inductance Coils
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: In the article the authors present the principle of operation of alternative maximum current protection (MCP) and protection against power cable earth faults. The purpose of these protections is the protection of high-voltage electrical installations, voltage 10-35kV from short circuits. These protections are performed without the use of current relays and current transformers (CTs) with metal cores widely used in the electric power industry, which have significant weight and dimensional parameters and high price cost. The proposed protection is made with the use of inductive coils, which have a number of known advantages for relay protection in comparison with CTs and other magnetosensitive elements and the possibility of their installation in the magnetic field created by the current- carrying busbar of the cell of the complete switchgear and closed switchgear. Protections with their application can be used instead of traditional current protections for various electrical installations, but at the same time by their technical and economic characteristics are not inferior to them. To expand the range of relay protection, the presented protections characterize an innovative approach in relay protection by using inductance coils. The resource-saving nature of these protections lies in the use of inductive coils, which are, both in terms of cost and weight and dimensional parameters, an order of magnitude cheaper and smaller in size and weight than the aforementioned CTs. The proposed protections are carried out in the form of structures with their installation inside the cells of complete switchgears and closed switchgears, voltage 10 and 35 kV.

articleTitle: Improving the Cyber-Security of the Electricity Demand-Response Aggregator Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The Demand Response (DR) Aggregator was created in the UES of Russia to manage the mechanism of price-dependent reduction of electricity consumption. The DR-Aggregator combines the resources of active consumers who have their own sources and/or energy storage, and the ability to shift their electricity consumption to off-peak hours. The DR-Aggregator has a hierarchical cluster structure, and consists of two closely interacting subsystems: technological and information-communication. Traditionally, the structure of the DR-Aggregator is managed centrally, information is collected and transmitted to devices in the control center by a communication environment through various communication channels, often insufficiently protected. It creates problems with confidentiality and security of data transmission because of cyber-attacks. The paper analyzes possible cyber-attacks on energy facilities included in the structure of the DR-Aggregator and on the demand management mechanism, suggests information protection measures, as well as technical and organizational measures aimed at improving cybersecurity during the operation of the DR-Aggregator.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Management Control of Line-to-Line Power Transfer in Automated Warehouse Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: Green logistics have been a trending research topic recently due to environmental challenges and energy optimization targets of that sector. Warehouses are considered the pillar of logistics and transportation sector operations since they act as a buffer between producers and consumers. A fully automated warehouse encompasses many devices and elements; however, stacker cranes are the key element in the product maneuvering processes. A battery-supported stacker crane can boost the system's sustainability by inducing autonomy. In order to prevent over-depletion of battery resources when a deficiency in generation is experienced, energy sharing between power lines of different cranes inside the warehouse is introduced. By employing an interlinking bidirectional DC converter, the burden of continuous active operation of certain crane systems can be shared with a crane that undergoes extended halt periods. In this research, the automated warehouse is considered as an islanded Microgrid where the energy is generated locally using a solar energy generator. The generation level fluctuation of the solar energy is tackled using the on-board battery systems of the crane units. Energy sharing is an operator-invoked functionality when inconsistency in the service tasks is observed between different service lines. A fuzzy logic management system is utilized to determine the required injected or extracted energy from the donor battery into the active line battery. Simulation of the power complex verified the effectiveness of the proposed design. Power sharing between the lines was maintained, while the load delivery response of the drive systems was not affected by the supply change.

articleTitle: Temperature Monitoring of Wind Turbines: Choosing the Optimal Method or Reliable Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The article discusses the problem of temperature control of components of wind turbine and conducts a comparative analysis of various methods of temperature measurement. The methods analyzed in the study are thermocouples, thermistors, infrared thermometers, and fiber optic sensors. Their accuracy, response speed, measurement range, reliability, cost-effectiveness, ease of installation, compatibility with existing systems and safety are assessed. As a result of the analysis, it was revealed that each method has its own advantages and limitations, depending on the specific application. Thermocouples and thermistors have shown high accuracy and sensitivity, but require direct contact with the surface being measured. IR thermometers provide fast, non-contact measurements but can be affected by environmental influences. Fiber optic sensors exhibit high accuracy and immunity to electromagnetic interference, but their installation can be complex and expensive.

articleTitle: Experience in Installing an Active High Harmonics Filter to Improve the Functioning of Specialized Medical Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The introduction of digital technologies into energy systems and the intellectualization of energy networks force us to pay increasing attention to the issues of power quality control. Due to the rapid technological development of electrical equipment, there is a need to find new approaches to solving problems of electromagnetic compatibility. This article discusses the main aspects related to the impact of power quality violations on the operation of electrical equipment, including specialized equipment for medical institutions. For medical institutions, despite the importance of complying with power quality indicators, there are no special requirements for their control. However, violations of power quality parameters lead to a decrease in the accuracy of displaying diagnostic results, which leads to distortions in the study and the occurrence of errors, which in some cases can be fatal. The State Autonomous Healthcare Institution “Interregional Clinical Diagnostic Center” of the city of Kazan was considered as the object of the study. As a result of a study of the dynamics of power quality indicators at particularly critical facilities of the Interregional Clinical Diagnostic Center, a deviation of the total harmonic component coefficient of currents THDi of up to 48% was revealed. To combat this violation, an active higher harmonic filter was selected and installed, which is a universal means of protection and can simultaneously perform several functions: reducing the level of higher harmonic components, power factor correction, reducing power losses, reducing flicker, etc. Installing an active harmonic filter reduced THDi to 2.5%, which is within the existing international standards.

articleTitle: Increased Effectiveness of Photovoltaic Power Stations for Frequency Control in Off-Grid Regions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: In many countries there are off-grid regions with different consumers that are not connected to the centralized power grid. Diesel power stations (DPS) based on diesel-generator units (DGU) having different capacity have traditionally been used for power supply in such regions. The mix of generating facilities is changing in off-grid regions following the global trend for decarbonization of the electricity generation sector. This is performed in the course of removal from operation of obsolete and worn diesel-generator units and putting into operation of renewable energy power generating facilities including hybrid power plants. Photovoltaic power stations (PV stations) play a significant role in this process. All PV stations are connected to power grids through inverters. The majority of PV stations utilize grid-tie inverters that require reference voltage from the grid to control their operation modes. Inverters can participate in frequency control within certain ranges. This is pre-determined by the algorithms included by the manufacturing plants to the automated control systems (ACS). The article covers the requirements set for the participation of PV stations in frequency control, the information about the protection settings of the inverters and the possibilities of their operation in emergency modes. The article also provides recommendations on the selection of the operation algorithms and the parameters for setting the PV station inverters. The necessity of using energy storage systems as part of the PV stations is substantiated with the view to improve the efficiency of the PV station participation in frequency control.

articleTitle: Bridging the Gap: Decision-Making Challenges in Smart Parking Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: This paper delves into a crucial yet overlooked facet of smart parking systems: critical decision-making. While existing research extensively covers routine processes such as car routing and scheduling, the focus on pivotal decisions has been lacking. Despite numerous studies, only 23 papers directly address critical decision-making, often not as their primary focus. This scarcity underscores the untapped potential for exploration in this domain. By conducting a comprehensive review, this paper not only highlights the existing research landscape but also identifies significant gaps. Moreover, it serves as a pioneering effort to shed light on the importance of critical decision-making in smart parking systems. By providing valuable insights and analysis, this review lays the groundwork for future research endeavors, encouraging scholars to delve deeper into this unexplored territory. In summary, this paper fills a notable void in the literature, paving the way for further advancements and understanding in the realm of smart parking system decision-making.

articleTitle: Development of a Mathematical Model of a Brushless Direct Current Motor Based on the Finit Element Method to Optimize Motor's Geometry
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: Brushless direct current motors are a class of electric machines that is dynamically developing. One of the directions of this development is related to the optimization of the geometry of the magnetic system, which provides high mass-energy performance. The existing mathematical models for optimization calculations based on the method of equivalent substitution schemes do not meet the requirements for the accuracy of determining the basic parameters. This reduces the quality of optimal design and slows down the development of electric drives. The purpose of the study: to develop a mathematical model that, on the one hand, would be simple, on the other hand, would have sufficient accuracy in determining the main energy parameters. Methods: the finite element method was chosen to build a mathematical model, but the number of elements into which the transverse geometry is divided is limited in advance. The model is parameterized and allows you to calculate any geometry. This approach allows you to create a simple and accurate model for optimization. Results: the technique is implemented in software code in the algorithmic Python language. The mathematical model includes 53 algebraic equations. The program takes into account the use of various electrical materials for electrical steel, high-coercive permanent magnets, copper armature windings. The mathematical model takes into account the lateral scattering fluxes of a permanent magnet, grooved scattering and scattering along the crowns of the teeth. Practical significance: the creation of a mathematical model with a limited number of elements is a new approach in electrical engineering. It allows you to make optimization calculations more accurate, thereby improving the mass-energy characteristics. This approach can be recommended for optimizing thermal conditions and aerodynamic calculations of electric machines. The proposed methodology will improve the design quality of brushless direct current motors and electric machines of other classes.

articleTitle: Ensuring the Safe Movement of Long-Distance AUVs in Conditions of Critical Energy Reserves
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: The movement of an autonomous uninhabited underwater vehicle along an extended route over a long period of time is considered. Due to the unpredictability of the external environment and losses in the power grid, actual energy consumption may differ significantly from the planned one, as a result of which the device may have a critical reserve of energy resources. The paper proposes an algorithm for identifying the state of the critical supply of energy resources using mathematical models of the most energy-intensive consumers. An algorithm for removing the device from the state of “critical energy reserve” is also proposed, for which it is proposed to generate in advance a list of optional consumers that can be gradually turned off or their operating mode changed. If the device is removed from the state of a critical energy resource, evaluate the possibility of fully or partially turning on previously disconnected equipment.

articleTitle: Resource-Saving Current Protections
publicationTitle: 2024 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: Works on creation of resource-saving protections without the use of measuring current transformers with metal cores have been carried out since the 60s of the 20th century. To build relay protection without measuring current transformers, in this work inductance coils and reed switches, which were magnetic field sensors, were used. Magnetic fields created by the currents of the current-carrying phases of complete switchgear cells have their maximum values in the immediate vicinity near the center of these busbars. These maximum values of magnetic fields in the form of EMFs are picked up inductance coils and reed switches. The reed switch and the inductance coil are installed in the location of the switchgear panel where the maximum magnetic induction is present. The inductance coil is the sensing element of the resource-saving protection. The reed switch is the sensing and actuating element of the resource-saving protection. Inductance coils and reed switches were chosen because, in comparison with other magnetically controlled elements, they have advantages for relay protection, such as: reed switches, for example, do not require amplifiers for signal transmission; the signal transmission itself is carried out through control circuits, not through measuring circuits; reed switches and inductance coils do not need temperature compensation devices. Reed switches can simultaneously act as an analog-to-discrete converter, a measuring converter and a measuring protection device. Inductance coils perform the functions of measuring converter and measuring protection body. The research relates to the protection of high-voltage electrical installations.
